summary.short: EU directive on privacy in electronic communications. Requires Member States to protect confidentiality of communications, regulates traffic and location data, cookies and terminal storage, directories, and unsolicited direct marketing, and imposes security duties on electronic communications service providers. Transposition due by 31 October 2003.
summary.long: Directive addressed to Member States (Art. 21); transposition due by 31 October 2003 (Art. 17). It particularises and complements Directive 95/46/EC for publicly available electronic communications services in public networks (Arts. 1-3). Providers must take security measures and warn subscribers of particular risks (Art. 4). Member States must ensure confidentiality of communications and traffic data, prohibit interception without consent, and condition storage of or access to terminal information on clear information and a right to refuse (Art. 5). Traffic data must be erased or anonymised when no longer needed, with limited billing uses and consent-based marketing uses (Art. 6). Location data other than traffic data may be processed only if anonymised or with consent, with a temporary refusal option (Art. 9). Calling and connected line identification must be restrictable, subject to tracing and emergency exceptions (Articles 8, 10); automatic call forwarding must be stoppable (Art. 11). Subscribers must be informed of and may control directory inclusion (Art. 12). Unsolicited direct marketing by automated calls, fax or email requires prior consent, subject to an existing-customer exception; disguised senders are prohibited (Art. 13). National restrictions for security and criminal enforcement are allowed (Art. 15). It repeals Directive 97/66/EC (Art. 19).

"user" means any natural person using a publicly available electronic communications service, for private or business purposes, without necessarily having subscribed to this service
"traffic data" means any data processed for the purpose of the conveyance of a communication on an electronic communications network or for the billing thereof

"location data" means any data processed in an electronic communications network, indicating the geographic position of the terminal equipment of a user of a publicly available electronic communications service
"communication" means any information exchanged or conveyed between a finite number of parties by means of a publicly available electronic communications service
"call" means a connection established by means of a publicly available telephone service allowing two-way communication in real time

definitions.defined_in: Directive 95/46/EC, by reference under Art. 2(f) of this Directive

evidence.quote: "consent" by a user or subscriber corresponds to the data subject's consent in Directive 95/46/EC

"value added service" means any service which requires the processing of traffic data or location data other than traffic data beyond what is necessary for the transmission of a communication or the billing thereof

"electronic mail" means any text, voice, sound or image message sent over a public communications network which can be stored in the network or in the recipient's terminal equipment until it is collected by the recipient

definitions.defined_in: Directive 2002/21/EC (Framework Directive), by general reference in the first paragraph of Art. 2

obligations.summary: Providers of publicly available electronic communications services must take appropriate technical and organisational measures to safeguard security of their services, at a level appropriate to the risk.

evidence.quote: must take appropriate technical and organisational measures to safeguard security of its services

obligations.summary: In case of a particular network security risk, the provider must inform subscribers of the risk and of any possible remedies, including likely costs.
obligations.conditional_on: In case of a particular risk of a breach of the security of the network

evidence.quote: must inform the subscribers concerning such risk

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure confidentiality of communications and related traffic data through national legislation.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure the confidentiality of communications and the related traffic data

obligations.summary: Listening, tapping, storage or other interception or surveillance of communications and related traffic data by persons other than users, without user consent, is prohibited except when legally authorised under Art. 15(1).
obligations.conditional_on: Except when legally authorised in accordance with Article 15(1)

evidence.quote: they shall prohibit listening, tapping, storage or other kinds of interception or surveillance of communications and the related traffic data by persons other than users

obligations.summary: Storing information in, or gaining access to information in, a subscriber's or user's terminal equipment is allowed only if the user is given clear and comprehensive information and offered the right to refuse, with listed technical or requested-service exceptions.
obligations.conditional_on: Excludes technical storage for the sole purpose of transmission or an information society service explicitly requested by the user

evidence.quote: is only allowed on condition that the subscriber or user concerned is provided with clear and comprehensive information

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure that terminal storage or access is conditional on information and a right to refuse, as stated in Art. 5(3).

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that the use of electronic communications networks to store information or to gain access to information stored in the terminal equipment

obligations.summary: Traffic data processed and stored by the provider must be erased or made anonymous when no longer needed for transmission, subject to Art. 6(2), (3), (5) and Art. 15(1).

evidence.quote: must be erased or made anonymous when it is no longer needed for the purpose of the transmission of a communication

obligations.summary: Traffic data necessary for subscriber billing and interconnection payments may be processed, only up to the end of the period during which the bill may lawfully be challenged or payment pursued.

evidence.quote: Traffic data necessary for the purposes of subscriber billing and interconnection payments may be processed.

obligations.summary: Traffic data may be processed for marketing or value added services only with the subscriber's or user's consent, which can be withdrawn at any time.
obligations.conditional_on: Only if the subscriber or user to whom the data relate has given consent

evidence.quote: if the subscriber or user to whom the data relate has given his/her consent

obligations.summary: The service provider must inform subscribers or users of the types of traffic data processed and the duration of processing for billing and, before obtaining consent, for marketing and value added services.

evidence.quote: The service provider must inform the subscriber or user of the types of traffic data which are processed

obligations.summary: Processing of traffic data must be restricted to persons acting under the authority of the provider handling billing, traffic management, customer enquiries, fraud detection, marketing or value added services, and to what is necessary.

evidence.quote: Processing of traffic data, in accordance with paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4, must be restricted to persons acting under the authority of providers

obligations.summary: Subscribers have the right to receive non-itemised bills.

evidence.quote: Subscribers shall have the right to receive non-itemised bills.

obligations.summary: Member States must apply national provisions to reconcile subscribers' itemised-bill rights with the privacy rights of calling users and called subscribers.

evidence.quote: Member States shall apply national provisions in order to reconcile the rights of subscribers receiving itemised bills

obligations.summary: Where calling or connected line identification is offered, the provider must offer callers and called subscribers free, simple means to prevent presentation of line identification, and to reject calls from withheld identification, per call or per line as specified.
obligations.conditional_on: Where presentation of calling or connected line identification is offered

evidence.quote: the service provider must offer the calling user the possibility, using a simple means and free of charge, of preventing the presentation of the calling line identification

obligations.summary: Providers must inform the public and subscribers about calling and connected line identification and the related privacy options.
obligations.conditional_on: Where presentation of calling and/or connected line identification is offered

evidence.quote: the providers of publicly available electronic communications services inform the public thereof

obligations.summary: Location data other than traffic data may be processed only if anonymised or with user consent for value added services; the provider must inform users before consent and allow withdrawal of consent.
obligations.conditional_on: Only where location data other than traffic data can be processed

evidence.quote: such data may only be processed when they are made anonymous, or with the consent of the users or subscribers

obligations.summary: Where consent to location data processing has been obtained, the user must continue to have a simple, free means of temporarily refusing processing for each connection or transmission.
obligations.conditional_on: Where consent has been obtained for processing of location data other than traffic data

evidence.quote: the user or subscriber must continue to have the possibility, using a simple means and free of charge, of temporarily refusing the processing

obligations.summary: Processing of location data other than traffic data must be restricted to persons acting under the authority of the network or service provider or the value added service provider.

evidence.quote: Processing of location data other than traffic data in accordance with paragraphs 1 and 2 must be restricted to persons acting under the authority

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure transparent procedures governing when providers may override calling line identification elimination (malicious calls) and location data consent (emergency services).

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that there are transparent procedures governing the way in which a provider

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure subscribers can stop automatic call forwarding by a third party to their terminal, using a simple, free means.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that any subscriber has the possibility, using a simple means and free of charge, of stopping automatic call forwarding

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure subscribers are informed free of charge before inclusion in public directories, can determine whether and which data are included, and that legitimate interests of non-natural persons are protected.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure that subscribers are informed, free of charge and before they are included in the directory

obligations.summary: Member States may require additional consent from subscribers for public directory purposes other than searching contact details by name and minimal identifiers.
obligations.conditional_on: For any purpose of a public directory other than the search of contact details of persons on the basis of their name

evidence.quote: Member States may require that for any purpose of a public directory other than the search of contact details

obligations.summary: Automated calling systems, fax or electronic mail for direct marketing may only be used in respect of subscribers who have given prior consent.

evidence.quote: may only be allowed in respect of subscribers who have given their prior consent

obligations.summary: Where a firm obtains customers' electronic contact details in a sale, it may use them for its own similar direct marketing if customers are given a free, easy opportunity to object at collection and in each message.
obligations.conditional_on: Where a natural or legal person obtains electronic contact details from customers in the context of a sale of a product or service

evidence.quote: customers clearly and distinctly are given the opportunity to object, free of charge and in an easy manner

obligations.summary: Member States must take appropriate measures ensuring that unsolicited direct marketing communications in other cases require consent or respect opt-out choices, and must ensure protection of non-natural persons' legitimate interests.
obligations.conditional_on: In cases other than those referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2

evidence.quote: Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that, free of charge, unsolicited communications for purposes of direct marketing

evidence.quote: the practice of sending electronic mail for purposes of direct marketing disguising or concealing the identity of the sender

obligations.summary: Member States must ensure no mandatory technical feature requirements are imposed on terminal or electronic communication equipment that would impede market placement and free circulation.

evidence.quote: Member States shall ensure, subject to paragraphs 2 and 3, that no mandatory requirements for specific technical features are imposed

evidence.quote: Member States shall inform the Commission in accordance with the procedure provided for by Directive 98/34/EC

obligations.summary: Measures may be adopted to ensure terminal equipment is constructed compatibly with users' right to protect and control the use of their personal data.

evidence.quote: measures may be adopted to ensure that terminal equipment is constructed in a way that is compatible

obligations.summary: Member States may adopt legislative measures restricting the scope of rights and obligations in Arts. 5, 6, 8(1)-(4) and 9, including data retention for a limited period, for national security, defence, public security and criminal law purposes.

evidence.quote: Member States may adopt legislative measures to restrict the scope of the rights and obligations provided for in Article 5

evidence.quote: shall also carry out the tasks laid down in Article 30 of that Directive

evidence.quote: Before 31 October 2003 Member States shall bring into force the provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.
